title: The Longest Cycle When Every Node Points to One Other

concept.title: Follow the only edge from each unvisited node; meeting a node of the current walk means you found a cycle
body: In this graph every node has **at most one outgoing edge** (a *functional graph*): a walk from a node is forced, there is nothing to choose. Each walk either ends at a node without an outgoing edge, or enters a **cycle**, and since every node leads to one next node, every cycle is a separate "loop" with trees of nodes hanging on it. We want the length of the longest cycle, or -1 if there is none.

Walk from every node that has not been visited yet, and keep, for every node on the **current walk**, the step number at which the walk reached it. Mark the nodes with the number of the walk that visited them. When the walk reaches a node that was visited by an **earlier** walk (or a dead end), it stops without a cycle. When it reaches a node that was visited by **the same walk**, it has closed a cycle, and the length is `current step - the step at which that node was first visited`.

body.code:
walk = [0] * (n + 1)                  # which walk visited the node (0 = none)
step = [0] * (n + 1)                  # the step number inside that walk
best = -1
for start in range(1, n + 1):
    if walk[start]:
        continue
    v, t = start, 0
    while v != 0 and not walk[v]:
        walk[v], step[v] = start, t
        t += 1
        v = next_node[v]
    if v != 0 and walk[v] == start:      # we came back to a node of this walk
        best = max(best, t - step[v])

body: Every node is visited once, so the time is O(n), and there is no recursion: a chain of 20000 nodes is handled by the loop.

statement: A directed graph has `n` nodes, and every node has at most one outgoing edge: `next[i]` is the node that the edge from `i` leads to, or 0 if there is none. A cycle is a closed walk that does not repeat a node. Print the number of nodes of the longest cycle, or -1 if the graph has no cycle.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes (numbered 1 to n).
The second line has `n` numbers: `next[i]` is the node that the only outgoing edge of the node `i` leads to, or 0 if the node `i` has no outgoing edge.
outputFormat: Print the length of the longest cycle or -1.
constraints: A node has at most one outgoing edge (but any number of incoming edges).

examples.note: The nodes 2, 3, 4 form a cycle (2 to 3 to 4 to 2): 3.
The walk from 1 ends at the node 3, which has no edge: -1.

hints: Walk from each node that has not been visited, following the only edge.
Remember for each node on the current walk the step at which it was reached.
If the walk reaches a node of the same walk, the cycle length is the difference of the steps; use a different mark for every walk.

explanation: Each unvisited node starts a walk along the only outgoing edges, marking nodes with the walk number and the step; reaching a node of the same walk closes a cycle whose length is the difference of the steps.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
nxt = list(map(int, input().split()))

walk = [0] * (n + 1)
step = [0] * (n + 1)
best = -1
for start in range(1, n + 1):
    if walk[start]:
        continue
    v = start
    t = 0
    while v != 0 and not walk[v]:
        walk[v] = start
        step[v] = t
        t += 1
        v = nxt[v - 1]
    if v != 0 and walk[v] == start:
        best = max(best, t - step[v])
print(best)
